articles.title: How to Write Payment Terms a Finance Team Can Actually Act On
articles.excerpt: How to Write Payment Terms a Finance Team Can Actually Act On The person who pays your invoice has never met you. They process forty documents a day against rules you did not write, and their incentiv…
articles.body: How to Write Payment Terms a Finance Team Can Actually Act On The person who pays your invoice has never met you. They process forty documents a day against rules you did not write, and their incentive is to clear the queue without making a mistake. Anything unusual about your invoice becomes an exception, and exceptions wait. That is what payment terms are for. Not decoration, not legal theatre — they are the instructions that let a stranger pay you correctly on the first attempt. Most late payments are not refusals. They are processing failures that better wording prevents. The four questions the terms block must answer If your terms do not answer all four in plain language, expect a delay: When exactly is payment due? A date, not a vibe. How do I pay, and what reference do I use?
articles.author: Karactif Tech

articles.title: Invoice Numbering: Gaps, Restarts, and the Mistakes That Cost You at Year End
articles.excerpt: Invoice Numbering: Gaps, Restarts, and the Mistakes That Cost You at Year End A freelance designer sends invoice #14 in March. In April she sends #14 again — different client, same number — because sh…
articles.body: Invoice Numbering: Gaps, Restarts, and the Mistakes That Cost You at Year End A freelance designer sends invoice #14 in March. In April she sends #14 again — different client, same number — because she duplicated last month's file and changed the amount but not the number. Nobody notices for eight months. Then her accountant tries to reconcile the year, finds two #14s and one missing #12, and the cleanup costs her a weekend and an awkward email to a client's finance team. The invoice number is the least glamorous field on the document and the one doing the most structural work: it is the join key between the invoice, the payment, the email thread and your books. Get it right once and it costs nothing for years. Get it wrong and you cannot fix it retroactively without creating more mess.
articles.author: Karactif Tech

articles.title: Building a website builder where every instruction is undoable
articles.excerpt: Most website builders treat an edit as a mutation. You change a heading, move a photo, swap a colour, and the previous version is gone unless you remembered to snapshot the whole page. That works when…
articles.body: Most website builders treat an edit as a mutation. You change a heading, move a photo, swap a colour, and the previous version is gone unless you remembered to snapshot the whole page. That works when you are clicking through a familiar UI. It gets brittle when the editor is a sentence: "make the photos bigger", "move the phone number to the top", "calmer". I wanted those sentences to be first-class objects, not disposable prompts. That is the idea behind silo.host: you describe the site in plain words, watch the layout, design and content change, and keep every instruction so you can undo any of them. Instructions are the history In a conventional CMS, the source of truth is the current document.

articles.body: Ever since the RAM crisis kicked off in earnest in November 2025, pretty much every component in a gaming PC has grown more expensive . Now, less than a month after the RTX 5080 hit $2,000 here in the US, it's reportedly going to get even more expensive in China. According to a post on ChannelGate , a Chinese tech insider board on WeChat, and spotted by Nvidia leaker Harukaze5719 on Twitter , MSI has increased GPU prices in China across the board, but the biggest increase is hitting the RTX 5080. Nvidia's penultimate GPU is going going up from 1,300 to 8,000 Yuan, or $194 to $1,199. However, lower-specced GPUs will have much less of a price increase, with the RTX 5060 only going up between 200 to 500 Yuan, or $30 to $75.

articles.title: Did comets bring building blocks of life to Earth? Scientists aren't so sure anymore
articles.excerpt: For over a century astronomers have speculated that comets could have delivered organic molecules necessary for life to Earth, but new modeling shows these molecules wouldn't have survived impact.
articles.body: The origin of life on Earth remains a mystery. New research shows that comets almost certainly did not bring the chemical building blocks of life to our planet. Life as we know it is based around carbon chemistry, also known as organic chemistry. Complex organic molecules are the fundamental building blocks of biochemical compounds such as nucleobases, amino acids, sugars and so on that act as the machinery for biochemistry on Earth . Two big questions are where did this complex chemistry originate? Did these complex organic molecules form on Earth, or were they delivered here from space?

articles.title: 'There's tremendous demand': Rocket Lab raises price of Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab has raised the launch cost of its next-gen Neutron rocket by more than 25%, an increase that reflects high demand amid a looming liftoff bottleneck.
articles.body: The coming launch bottleneck has ramped up demand for a rocket that has yet to leave the ground. Rocket Lab announced on Monday (Nov. 9) that it recently raised the price of a Neutron launch from $55 million to $70 million — an increase of more than 25%, for a ride on a rocket that's set to debut in 2027. "Launch is extremely constrained, and that is exactly the situation we predicted," Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said on Monday during the company's third-quarter earnings call.

articles.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
articles.excerpt: This dazzling collection of ancient stars could hold clues to the Milky Way's past.
articles.body: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus.

articles.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
articles.excerpt: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility.
articles.body: A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum.
articles.author: Robert Lea
